method.pipeline: D1_FORWARD -> D2_REVERSE -> D3_TRANCEPTION -> D4_SCALE -> D5_TIME_IDENTITY_PROVENANCE -> iNAIHR_CHALLENGE -> HRAIN_REINTEGRATION

internal_sources: Janus-Demiurge native cruise trackline gate PR12/latest scout summaries

reverse_spiral_nodes.claim: The principal JANUS HA10 waveform windows used for the 119-Hz confirmatory run, in-band positive control and December/January baseline diagnostics occur after the documented onset of the H10S electronic-noise/cross-talk fault.

evidence.known_fault_onset: 2013-07-19 electrical-noise spike on H10S1; evolved to strong permanent noise with cross-talk to H10S2 and H10S3
evidence.operations_change: H10S1 removed from IDC Operations after the fault because of high electronic noise/spurious detections

reverse_spiral_nodes.claim: During the known H10S1 fault epoch, H10S2 cannot be treated as an independently clean hydrophone without an explicit cross-talk control.

evidence.ctbto: Noise on H10S1 is documented to affect H10S2 and H10S3 through cross-talk, with varying periods of low and strong cross-talk.
evidence.janus: H10S2 shows much higher broadband baseline power than H10N1 and substantially lower event-vs-noise SNR in the positive control.

reverse_spiral_nodes.previous_overstrong_reading_to_avoid: A persistent S2/N1 offset alone is not sufficient to label the effect as seafloor/site resonance or a clean station gain difference.

reverse_spiral_nodes.claim: The documented StationXML response correction used by JANUS does not normalize the approximately 12-13 dB H10S2-over-H10N1 broadband baseline offset.

The routine post-deployment UWS calibration described by CTBTO measures digitizer electronics by injecting a known signal after switching out the hydrophone ceramic/analogue sensing path; it is not equivalent to a full at-sea end-to-end hydrophone+riser calibration.

evidence.predeployment: Full end-to-end calibration includes hydrophone sensing element/pre-amplifier and UWS digitizer electronics.
evidence.postdeployment: Known waveform injection is used to measure UWS digitizer response; CTBTO 2025 explicitly describes current deployed calibration as excluding the analogue hydrophone/riser contribution and motivates full-chain in-situ calibration.

reverse_spiral_nodes.claim: CTBTO/EGU material documents calibration-response changes around the 2013 H10S fault onset: H10S1 shifted by 0.8396 dB between March and September 2013, while H10S2/H10S3 before-vs-after comparisons show differences up to 4.7832 dB and 2.5340 dB in 1-100 Hz, with inverse trends relative to H10S1 and interpretation consistent with riser failure/cross-talk.
reverse_spiral_nodes.claim_ceiling: The text extraction does not safely assign which of the 4.7832 dB and 2.5340 dB maxima belongs specifically to H10S2 versus H10S3 without the figure-level channel labels; preserve both as the H10S2/H10S3 pair of reported maxima.

reverse_spiral_nodes.claim: The same CTBTO calibration study reports extremely small H10N digitizer-response differences between 2013 and 2017 (maximum differences of only a few thousandths of a dB in 1-100 Hz), while H10S shows the documented fault epoch.

CTBTO material states the Treaty amplitude-calibration requirement for IMS hydrophone stations as 1-100 Hz. The JANUS 119-Hz target lies above this band and near the 125-Hz Nyquist limit of the 250-Hz data.
CTBTO station history describes HA10 north and south triplets with very different trunk-cable lengths, approximately 20 km and 127 km respectively.
A calibration or cross-talk effect can alter the recorded acoustic contrast but cannot erase a physical seabed structure from independent bathymetry/backscatter data.

evidence.current_native_track_gate: No exact public machine-readable cruise-track crossing has yet been admitted for the frozen HA10 points in the latest scout pass.
evidence.mail_gates: BODC, BAS/PDC, BGS, UKHO, CTBTO/Fugro/NAVFAC requests remain active for native track, swath and historical survey provenance.

spiral_synthesis.A0_observation: H10S2 is approximately 12-13 dB higher than H10N1 across 10-80 Hz in multiple 2014-2015 samples.
spiral_synthesis.B0_reverse_parent: Those samples occur after a documented 2013 H10S1 electronic-noise fault with time-variable cross-talk into H10S2/H10S3.
spiral_synthesis.C0_countermodel: The S2 excess can therefore arise from contaminated south-triplet measurement-path noise without requiring a seabed-resonance explanation.
spiral_synthesis.ASCEND_1: StationXML correction barely changes the S2/N1 ratio, so the correction we applied is not what flattened or created the 12-13 dB offset.
spiral_synthesis.A1_identity_check: Routine deployed digitizer calibration is not a full hydrophone+riser-chain calibration, so a riser/analogue fault can survive nominal response correction.
spiral_synthesis.B1_historical_anchor: Published H10S calibration-response changes and cross-talk are temporally upstream of every main JANUS S2 waveform test inspected in this pass.
spiral_synthesis.C1_discriminator: Compare all three H10S channels against all three H10N channels before and after 2013-07-19 using raw counts first, then response-corrected data, and test whether S1 noise predicts S2/S3 excess/coherence.
spiral_synthesis.ASCEND_2: Only after the triplet-crosstalk gate and independent bathymetry/swath gate should residual acoustic morphology be interpreted as a candidate site/seafloor effect.

design: Freeze pre-fault windows before 2013-07-19 and post-fault windows including exact existing 2014-12/2015-01 JANUS windows where archive coverage permits.
Analyze RAW COUNTS first; apply response correction only as a second lane.
Measure fixed-band PSD, pairwise coherence/correlation and coincident transient-noise coupling without post-hoc frequency selection.
Test whether H10S1 noise level/coincident spikes predict H10S2/H10S3 excess and whether this relation is absent/weaker pre-fault and in H10N.
No claim about seabed structure may be promoted from this gate alone.
Obtain authoritative pre/post-2013 H10S1/S2/S3 calibration sequence dates and transfer functions.
Ask whether StationXML response epochs incorporate any fault-era correction or only nominal/system response.
Ask for H10S1 crosstalk/noise maintenance history and any riser-cable intervention/replacement dates.
Require an exact track/swath/coverage intersection before making local seabed-geometry claims.
Keep bathymetry/backscatter evidence independent from acoustic calibration evidence.

existing_request_already_asks: complete station/deployment metadata and station history
new_specific_followup_questions_to_hold_: Please provide the H10S1/H10S2/H10S3 calibration sequence timeline around 2013-07-19 and the following years.
Did any StationXML response epoch change because of the H10S1 electronic-noise/cross-talk fault?
Were H10S2/H10S3 data quality flags or operational exclusions applied during high-cross-talk periods?
Was the suspected H10S1 riser-cable failure ever repaired/replaced, and on what date?
Can the pre/post-fault UWS calibration transfer functions be shared numerically?

claim_ceiling: This reverse pass establishes that a documented H10S fault/cross-talk epoch is temporally upstream of the JANUS H10S2 analyses and that the routine response correction used by JANUS does not remove the observed S2/N1 offset. It does not prove that cross-talk caused the full offset, does not prove or disprove a physical seabed structure, and does not promote the 119-Hz target.
